headline.summary: The project has substantial research, an MVP implementation plan, service/domain framing and a provenance-aware ingestion architecture. The main gap is convergence into executable code: most core components are still documented rather than implemented.

project_streams.name: Product / MMP concept
project_streams.summary: MMP vocabulary, service tiers, sovereign reference-client framing, build semantics and ADRs are documented.
project_streams.next: Resolve governance/verification questions and align terminology with the MVP plan.

project_streams.name: Municipality/service research
project_streams.summary: A 19-municipality qualitative survey, service taxonomy and Ausserberg/reference-service material exist.
project_streams.next: Turn research into fixtures/baseline corpus and acceptance scenarios.

project_streams.name: Data acquisition / ingestion pipeline
project_streams.summary: Adaptive crawling, provenance, semantic compiler, Apertus execution model and evaluation criteria are designed; runtime code is not yet committed.
project_streams.next: Baseline corpus → SourceSnapshot → PageIR → HTTP-first fetch → typed planner/executor.

project_streams.name: Hackathon MVP implementation
project_streams.summary: A detailed 24-hour plan defines URL→inventory→review→MCP package, but the repository currently has only a minimal Python package skeleton.
project_streams.next: Start executable vertical slice using Ausserberg + second municipality.

project_streams.name: MCP runtime
project_streams.summary: Tool contract and runtime shape are planned; no MCP server implementation is visible in main.
project_streams.next: Fixture-backed four-tool MCP server, then wire generated inventory.

project_streams.name: Citizen / team UX
project_streams.summary: Open WebUI/reference-client and a minimal builder page are proposed; no UI implementation is visible.
project_streams.next: Validate host integration first; keep builder UI minimal.

project_streams.name: Quality / trust / Judge
project_streams.summary: Evidence discipline, withheld attributes, build floor and eval criteria are well described but not automated.
project_streams.next: Turn evidence checks and acceptance criteria into executable tests.

project_streams.name: Deployment / go-to-market
project_streams.summary: Hosted HTTPS demo, downloadable package and adoption framing are planned; no deployment artifact is visible.
project_streams.next: Choose hosting and prove clean package launch before polish.

open_questions.question: Which architectural source is authoritative when the MVP plan and MMP/ADR documents differ?
Who owns the first end-to-end executable slice: crawl/extraction, MCP runtime, and integration?
Can Apertus reliably call the MCP tools and perform constrained extraction/classification at the required quality?
When will the municipality baseline/reference corpus be committed and linked to acceptance tests?
Is eCH-0070 a hackathon dependency, later enrichment, or canonical identity layer? Current docs are not fully aligned.
Does a municipality need sign-off before publication, and who is publisher of record?
Which crawler/runtime do we standardize on for the first slice: Crawl4AI or thinner HTTP + Playwright?

next_actions: Converge the team on one MVP contract: URL → evidence-backed service inventory → MCP.
Merge/review PR #3 and make its ingestion boundaries part of the shared implementation plan.
Commit the baseline/reference corpus and convert Ausserberg + selected municipalities into fixtures.
Build the first executable vertical slice: fetch → snapshot → extract → validate → inventory.
Bring up a fixture MCP server with the four planned tools and test a real host/model.
Turn provenance/Judge principles into automated acceptance checks.
Keep the observatory repo-wide and refresh it from Git + project evidence, not manual optimism.

tensions.title: MVP scope vs. richer MMP architecture
tensions.detail: The MVP plan explicitly excludes Dominik's documents from its design, while the wider project contains MMP vocabulary, ADRs and quality/governance concepts. The team needs to decide which parts converge now versus remain post-hackathon.

tensions.title: Commercial baseline vs. Apertus goal
tensions.detail: The MVP plan uses commercial LLMs for build-time extraction first; the pipeline design aims for a large-planner/small-Apertus execution architecture. This is compatible if treated as baseline → replacement experiment, but should be stated explicitly.

tensions.title: eCH-0070 timing
tensions.detail: Research recommends eCH-0070 as canonical service identity; the MVP plan treats it as later enrichment. This is an explicit architectural decision still needing alignment.
